newsitem.title: INDIA: Experimental India nuclear reactor goes critical.
newsitem.headline: Experimental India nuclear reactor goes critical.

text.p: India on Tuesday inaugurated an experimental nuclear reactor which uses the man-made element Uranium 233 as fuel, the country's apex nuclear research body said in a statement.
The 30 KW rated reactor, Kamini, located at Kalpakkam in the southern state of Tamil Nadu, reached criticality at 11.58 a.m. on Monday, the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) said.
"This is an important milestone along the path to extracting the vast energy locked in India's thorium reserves," Dr Anil Kakodkar, the nuclear scientist who heads the BARC, told Reuters.
Kakodkar said that U-233 is obtained by irradiating thorium. Thorium, in the form of monazite, is found on the beaches of the southern state of Kerala. India has vast reserves of monazite.
Utilising these reserves is key to sustaining the Indian nuclear power generation programme, the BARC statement said.
Kamini is the seventh of India's research reactors. These include the oldest, Apsara, a one MW swimming-pool reactor, and Dhruva, a 100 MW rated research reactor.
Kadkokar said Kamini was the only reactor using U-233 as fuel in the world at present.
"During the early days of nuclear research, there were some," he said. "Now there are none."
But the U-233 technology could not immediately be harnessed to generate nuclear power, Kakodkar said.
"That will take quite some time," he said. "We are designing a 200 MW electric power reactor at the moment."
India has nine nuclear reactors generating a total of just under 2000 MW of power, officials said.
Kakodkar said the Kamini reactor would be used for experiments in neutron radiography, and in the testing of nuclear detectors and other instruments for automobile and space technology.
The Press Trust of India newsagency quoted Dr R Chidambaram, chairman of India's Atomic Energy Commission, as saying the reactor cost around $280,500 to construct.
